newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedes more optimistic about economy - poll.
newsitem.headline: Swedes more optimistic about economy - poll.

text.p: Swedish households' expectations about the economy have improved in the past few months, a survey by pollster SKOP showed on Wednesday.

At the time of the survey, 14 percent of households believed their standard of living would improve in the coming year compared to 13 percent a month earlier. The number who believe their standard of living would fall dropped to 27 percent from 30.
The survey, conducted between January 17 and February 7, polled 1,000 Swedes.

"Households' expectations about the economy have improved in the past few months. In January/February, 24 percent of those surveyed believed the economic situation in Sweden would improve in the coming year against 23 percent in December 1996.
"Some 39 percent believe the economy would worsen compared to 44 percent in December," it said.

It said in 1997 households may continue to be careful spenders because of their growing fear of unemployment. The poll showed 51 percent of Swedes believed the jobless rate would increase compared to 46 percent a month ago.
